[in LXX: ⟦Jeremiah 46:5|Je 26 (46):5⟧ (⁨סוּג⁩), II Mac 4:33, III Mac 2:33*;] ⟪to go away⟫, ⟪depart⟫, ⟪withdraw⟫: seq. ἀπό, ⟦Matthew 7:23|Mt 7:23⟧, ⟦Luke 9:39|Lk 9:39⟧, ⟦Acts 13:13|Ac 13:13⟧ (absol., ⟦Luke 20:20|Lk 20:20⟧, Tr., mg.).†

G673.b:
⟪ἀπο-χωρίζω⟫,
[in LXX: ⟦Ezekiel 43:21|Ez 43:21⟧ (⁨מִפְקָד⁩)*;] ⟪to separate⟫, ⟪part asunder⟫: pass., ⟦Revelation 6:14|Re 6:14⟧; reflexively, ⟪to separate oneself⟫: ⟦Acts 15:39|Ac 15:39⟧.†

G674.b:
** ⟪ἀπο-ψύχω⟫,
[in LXX: IV Mac 15:18*;]
⟪1.⟫ ⟪to breathe out life⟫, ⟪expire⟫ (Thuc.; LXX, IV Mac 15:18).
⟪2.⟫ ⟪to leave off breathing⟫, ⟪faint⟫ (Hom., Od., xxiv, 348): seq. ἀπό, ⟦Luke 21:26|Lk 21:26⟧.†

G675.b: ⟪Ἄππιος⟫, -ου, ὁ, ⟪Appius⟫; Ἀππίου Φόρον, Appii Forum (Market of Appius), a town in Italy: ⟦Acts 28:15|Ac 28:15⟧.†

G676.b:
*† ⟪ἀ-πρόσ-ιτος⟫, -ον
(< πρόσειμι, to go to), ⟪unapproachable⟫: φῶς, ⟦1 Timothy 6:16|I Ti 6:16⟧.†

G677.b:
**† ⟪ἀπρόσκοπος⟫, -ον
(< προσκόπτω), [in LXX: Si 35 (32):21, III Mac 3:8*;]
⟪1.⟫ act., ⟪not causing to stumble⟫: metaph., of not leading others into sin, ⟦1 Corinthians 10:32|I Co 10:32⟧.
⟪2.⟫ Pass., ⟪not stumbling⟫, ⟪without offence⟫, ⟪blameless⟫: ⟦Acts 24:16|Ac 24:16⟧, ⟦Philippians 1:10|Phl 1:10⟧ (for exx., v. MM, s.v.).†

G678.b:
*† ⟪ἀπροσωπολήμπτως⟫ (Rec. -λήπτως, cl.), adv.
(< α- neg., προσωπολήμπτης), ⟪without respect of persons⟫, ⟪impartially⟫: ⟦1 Peter 1:17|I Pe 1:17⟧.†

G679.b:
** ⟪ἄ-πταιστος⟫, -ον
(< πταίω), [in LXX: III Mac 6:39*;] ⟪without stumbling⟫, ⟪sure-footed⟫: metaph. (MM, s.v.), ⟦Jude 1:24|Ju 24⟧.†

G681.b:
⟪ἅπτω⟫,
[in LXX chiefly for ⁨נגע⁩;] prop., ⟪to fasten to⟫; hence, of fire, ⟪to kindle⟫, ⟪light⟫: ⟦Luke 8:16|Lk 8:16⟧ ⟦Luke 11:33|11:33⟧ ⟦Luke 15:8|15:8⟧, ⟦Acts 28:2|Ac 28:2⟧. Mid., c. gen., ⟪to fasten oneself to⟫, ⟪cling to⟫, ⟪lay hold of⟫ (so in π.; MM, s.v.): ⟦Matthew 8:3|Mt 8:3⟧, ⟦Matthew 8:15|15⟧, ⟦John 20:17|Jo 20:17⟧, al.; of carnal intercourse, ⟦1 Corinthians 7:1|I Co 7:1⟧; with reference to levitical and ceremonial prohibitions, ⟦2 Corinthians 6:17|II Co 6:17⟧, ⟦Colossians 2:21|Col 2:21⟧; of hostile action, ⟦1 John 5:18|I Jo 5:18⟧ (cf. ἀν-, καθ-, περι- άπτω).
SYN.: θιγγάνω, ψηλαφάω. ἅ. is the stronger, θ., to touch, the lighter term. ψ. is to feel, as in search of something (Tr., Syn., § xvii; Lft., Col., 201 f.).
a: Commentaries on St. Paul's Epistles to the Galatians (1892); Philippians (Third Edition, 1873); and Colossians and Philemon (1892), by J. B. Lightfoot. Macmilian. Also Apostolic Fathers, by the same. 5 vols. Macmilian, 1890
Synonyms of the N. T. , by R. C. Trench. Ninth Edition. Macmillan, 1880

G683.b:
⟪ἀπ-ωθέω⟫, -ῶ,
[in LXX for ⁨זנח⁩, ⁨מאס⁩, etc.;] ⟪to thrust away⟫. Mid., ⟪to thrust away from oneself⟫, ⟪refuse⟫, reject: c. acc. pers. (MM, s.v.), ⟦Acts 7:27|Ac 7:27⟧, ⟦Acts 7:39|39⟧ ⟦Acts 13:46|13:46⟧, ⟦Romans 11:1|Ro 11:1⟧, ⟦Romans 11:2|2⟧, ⟦1 Timothy 1:19|I Ti 1:19⟧.†

G684.b:
⟪ἀπώλεια⟫, -ας, ἡ
(< ἀπόλλυμι), [in LXX (Cremer, 797) for ⁨אבד⁩, ⁨אֵיד⁩, etc.;] ⟪destruction⟫, ⟪waste⟫, ⟪loss⟫, ⟪perishing⟫ (in π., of money, v. MM, s.v.): ⟦Matthew 26:8|Mt 26:8⟧, ⟦Mark 14:4|Mk 14:4⟧, ⟦Acts 8:20|Ac 8:20⟧, ⟦Romans 9:22|Ro 9:22⟧, ⟦1 Timothy 6:9|I Ti 6:9⟧, ⟦2 Peter 2:1|II Pe 2:1⟧; in special sense of the loss of eternal life, ⟪perdition⟫, the antithesis of σωτηρία: ⟦Matthew 7:13|Mt 7:13⟧, ⟦John 17:12|Jo 17:12⟧, ⟦Philippians 1:28|Phl 1:28⟧ ⟦Philippians 3:19|3:19⟧, ⟦2 Thessalonians 2:3|II Th 2:3⟧, ⟦Hebrews 10:39|He 10:39⟧, ⟦2 Peter 2:3|II Pe 2:3⟧ ⟦2 Peter 3:7|3:7⟧, ⟦2 Peter 3:16|16⟧, ⟦Revelation 17:8|Re 17:8⟧, ⟦Revelation 17:11|11⟧ (DB, iii, 744).†
a: Biblico-Theological Lexicon of N.T. Greek, by H. Cremer. Third English Edition, with Supplement. T. & T. Clark, 1886

G686.b: ⟪ἄρα⟫, illative particle, expressing a more subjective or informal inference than οὖν, ⟪then⟫: prop. (as in cl.), the second word in the sentence, ⟦Romans 7:21|Ro 7:21⟧ ⟦Romans 8:1|8:1⟧, ⟦Galatians 3:7|Ga 3:7⟧; ἐπεὶ ἄρα, ⟦1 Corinthians 7:14|I Co 7:14⟧ (with another word between) ⟦1 Corinthians 5:10|5:10⟧; as the first word, ⟦Luke 11:48|Lk 11:48⟧, ⟦Acts 11:18|Ac 11:18⟧, ⟦Romans 10:17|Ro 10:17⟧, ⟦1 Corinthians 15:18|I Co 15:18⟧, ⟦2 Corinthians 5:15|II Co 5:15⟧ ⟦2 Corinthians 7:12|7:12⟧, ⟦Hebrews 4:9|He 4:9⟧; so prop. in apodosis after protasis with εἰ, ⟦Matthew 12:28|Mt 12:28⟧, ⟦Luke 11:20|Lk 11:20⟧, ⟦Galatians 2:21|Ga 2:21⟧ ⟦Galatians 3:29|3:29⟧ ⟦Galatians 5:11|5:11⟧, ⟦Hebrews 12:8|He 12:8⟧ (κενὸν ἄρα), ⟦1 Corinthians 15:14|I Co 15:14⟧; often in interrogations, direct and indirect, τίς (τί) ἄρα, ⟦Matthew 18:1|Mt 18:1⟧ ⟦Matthew 19:25|19:25⟧, ⟦Matthew 19:27|27⟧ ⟦Matthew 24:45|24:45⟧, ⟦Mark 4:41|Mk 4:41⟧, ⟦Luke 1:66|Lk 1:66⟧ ⟦Luke 8:25|8:25⟧ ⟦Luke 12:42|12:42⟧ ⟦Luke 22:23|22:23⟧, ⟦Acts 12:18|Ac 12:18⟧; εἰ ἄρα, ⟦Mark 11:13|Mk 11:13⟧, ⟦Acts 8:22|Ac 8:22⟧; εἴπερ ἄρα, ⟦1 Corinthians 15:15|I Co 15:15⟧; οὐκ ἄρα, ⟦Acts 21:38|Ac 21:38⟧; μήτι ἄρα, ⟦2 Corinthians 1:17|II Co 1:17⟧; in strengthened forms, ἄρα γε, ἄραγε, ⟦Matthew 7:20|Mt 7:20⟧ ⟦Matthew 17:26|17:26⟧, ⟦Acts 17:27|Ac 17:27⟧, and more freq. ἄρα οὖν (Epp. Paul.), ⟪so then⟫, ⟦Romans 5:18|Ro 5:18⟧ ⟦Romans 7:3|7:3⟧, ⟦Romans 7:25|25⟧ ⟦Romans 8:12|8:12⟧ ⟦Romans 9:16|9:16⟧, ⟦Romans 9:18|18⟧ ⟦Romans 14:12|14:12⟧, ⟦Romans 14:19|19⟧, ⟦Galatians 6:10|Ga 6:10⟧, ⟦Ephesians 2:19|Eph 2:19⟧, ⟦1 Thessalonians 5:6|I Th 5:6⟧, ⟦2 Thessalonians 2:15|II Th 2:15⟧ (Bl., § 77, 2; 78, 5; MM, s.v.).†

G687.b:
⟪ἆρα⟫, interrog. particle, implying anxiety or impatience, "quite rare and only in Luke and Paul, therefore a literary word" (Bl., §77, 2).
⟪1.⟫ (num igitur) expecting a neg. reply, ⟦Luke 18:8|Lk 18:8⟧; ἆρά γε, ⟦Acts 8:30|Ac 8:30⟧.
⟪2.⟫ (ergone) in apodosis, expecting an affirm. reply, ⟦Galatians 2:17|Ga 2:17⟧ (Bl., §77, 2; Lft., Ga., in l.; MM, s.v.).†
a: Commentaries on St. Paul's Epistles to the Galatians (1892); Philippians (Third Edition, 1873); and Colossians and Philemon (1892), by J. B. Lightfoot. Macmilian. Also Apostolic Fathers, by the same. 5 vols. Macmilian, 1890

G685.b:
⟪ἀρά⟫, -ᾶς, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for ⁨אלה⁩];
⟪1.⟫ ⟪a prayer⟫ (MM, s.v.).
⟪2.⟫ (as in Homer) ⟪a curse⟫, ⟪malediction⟫: ⟦Romans 3:14|Ro 3:14⟧(LXX).†

a: The N.T. in the original Greek, by B. F. Westcott and F. J. A. Hort. Vol. II, Introduction and Appendix. Macmillan, 1881

G691.b:
⟪ἀργέω⟫, -ῶ
(< ἀργός), [in LXX: ⟦Ezra 4:24|Es 4:24⟧, ⟦Ecclesiastes 12:3|Ec 12:3⟧ (⁨בּטל⁩), I Es 2:30, Si 30:36 (33:27), II Mac 5:25*;] ⟪to be idle⟫; τὸ κρίμα . . . ἀ., ⟪lingers⟫ (cf. MGr. ἀργά, ⟪late⟫: MM, s.v.): ⟦2 Peter 2:3|II Pe 2:3⟧.†

G692.b:
⟪ἀργός⟫, -όν
(in late Gk., incl. NT, -ή, -όν; < ἀ- neg., ἔργον), [in LXX: ⟦1 Kings 6:7|III Ki 6:7⟧ (⁨מַסָּע⁩?), Wi 14:5 15:15, Si 37:11 38:28*;] ⟪inactive⟫, ⟪idle⟫: ⟦Matthew 20:3|Mt 20:3⟧, ⟦Matthew 20:6|6⟧, ⟦1 Timothy 5:13|I Ti 5:13⟧, ⟦Titus 1:12|Tit 1:12⟧, ⟦2 Peter 1:8|II Pe 1:8⟧. Metaph., of things, ⟪inactive⟫, ⟪ineffective⟫, ⟪worthless⟫: ῥῆμα, ⟦Matthew 12:36|Mt 12:36⟧; πίστις, ⟦James 2:20|Ja 2:20⟧ (v. Cremer, 259 f.).†
SYN.: βραδύς, slow; νωθρός, sluggish (Tr., Syn., § civ).

G693.b:
⟪ἀργύρεος⟫ (v. MM, s.v.), -οῦς, -ᾶ, -οῦν
(< ἄργυρος), [in LXX for ⁨כֶּסֶף⁩;] ⟪of silver⟫: ⟦Acts 19:24|Ac 19:24⟧ (WH, br.), ⟦2 Timothy 2:20|II Ti 2:20⟧, ⟦Revelation 9:20|Re 9:20⟧.†

G695.b:
† ⟪ἀργυροκόπος⟫, -ου, ὁ
(< ἄργυρος, κόπτω, to beat), [in LXX: ⟦Judges 17:4|Jg 17:4⟧, ⟦Jeremiah 6:29|Je 6:29⟧ (⁨צֹרֵף⁩)*;] ⟪a silversmith⟫: ⟦Acts 19:24|Ac 19:24⟧ (Plut.; π., v. MM, s.v.).†

G696.b:
⟪ἄργυρος⟫, -ου, ὁ
(< ἀργός, shining), [in LXX for ⁨כֶּסֶף⁩;] ⟪silver⟫ (on its relation to ἀργύριον, v. MM, s.v.): ⟦Matthew 10:9|Mt 10:9⟧, ⟦Acts 17:29|Ac 17:29⟧, ⟦James 5:5|Ja 5:5⟧, ⟦Revelation 18:12|Re 18:12⟧.†

G697.b: ⟪Ἄρειος Πάγος⟫ (T, Ἄριος Π.), -ου, ὁ, ⟪Hill of Ares⟫ or ⟪Mars⟫, ⟪Areopagus⟫; also, ⟪the Court of Areopagus⟫, the highest tribunal of Athens: ⟦Acts 17:19|Ac 17:19⟧, ⟦Acts 17:22|22⟧.†

G698.b: ⟪Ἀρεοπαγίτης⟫ (T, -είτης), -ου, ὁ (v. supr.), a judge of the Court of Areopagus: ⟦Acts 17:34|Ac 17:34⟧.†

G699.b:
⟪ἀρεσκία⟫ (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ
(< ἀρέσκω), [in LXX (-εία): ⟦Proverbs 31:30|Pr 31:30⟧ (⁨חֵן⁩)*;] ⟪pleasing⟫, ⟪desire to please⟫: ⟦Colossians 1:10|Col 1:10⟧. In Gk. writers (Arist., Polyb.), most freq. in bad sense, but in π., Inscr., and in Philo, as above (v. Deiss., BS, 224; MM, s.v.; Cremer, 642).†
